subject: Pilot candidate matrix + next asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot candidate matrix + next asks

Hi team,

Quick post-demo recap from the call with Rebecca/Samir at Acme earlier today and a proposed pilot candidate matrix. The goal: pick a 2–3 model slate we can surface to Acme for a 4-week pilot (production-like prompts + evals) and get a pricing anchor for procurement.

What I heard on the call (short):
- Primary workload: long-form personalization + structured extraction from support transcripts (~600 tokens average, peaks to 1,200).
- Latency requirement: p95 < 450ms for interactive segments, but batch/async OK for heavy extraction jobs.
- Quality guardrails: high precision on entity extraction, low hallucination for billing-related fields.
- Budget: not unlimited — procurement asked for a ballpark that demonstrates unit economics before committing to Dedicated.

Recommended pilot candidates (rationale summary):
1) Redwood-2.7B-q8
   - Why: best balance for interactive latency and cost. Expected p95 ~350ms with our continuous batching + KV caching. Quality passes entity extraction checks in our quick evals.
   - Tradeoffs: less headroom for adversarial creative prompts, may need conservative decoding params.
2) OpenLlama-13B-4bit (quantized)
   - Why: stronger on complex reasoning / multi-turn consistency. Better precision on structured extraction when tuned.
   - Tradeoffs: higher cost (~2.6x token cost), p95 ~700–900ms on a single GPU; suggest async/extraction workers or slicing into smaller sequences.
3) Redwood-7B-ptq (ops variant) — optional fallback
   - Why: mid-point on quality; cheaper than 13B, better quality than 2.7B for certain edge cases. Useful as automatic fallback when latency/throughput trades are enforced.

Attached: acme_benchmarks_v1.csv (pilot microbenchmarks), prompt_set_v2.zip (seed prompts + test prompts), MAP-Acme-2027.pdf (mutual action plan). Also added the eval run link in related_links.

Concrete asks / next steps:
- Engineering: run a short production-like benchmark using prompt_set_v2 (tail across 600–1,200 tokens) and return per-model p50/p95 token latency + cost-per-1000-tokens by EOD Friday. (Karthik)
- Solutions/Sales: confirm which prompts we should prioritize for the initial quality guardrails test (Marissa + Jonas).
- Commercial: produce a 4-week pilot quote and a simplified pricing anchor (Ben).
- Legal/Procurement: anticipate a standard pilot SOW and 30-day invoice cadence; contact procurement@acme.ai once price anchor is ready.

I recommend we lead with Redwood-2.7B-q8 + OpenLlama-13B-4bit as the two-test path, with Redwood-7B-ptq enabled as a fallback. That gives Acme clear options: low-latency cost-efficient path and a higher-quality path to compare on their real data.

I'll draft the external recap and next steps to send to Rebecca + Samir after engineering flags any blockers.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot candidate matrix + next asks

Jonas — quick engineering read. Thanks for the clear matrix. A few notes from infra benching perspective before we commit:

1) Latency expectations: our microbenchmarks line up with your numbers for 2.7B-q8 when KV cache hits are high. For cold prompts with 1,200 tokens we see p95 closer to ~520ms unless we tune batching and ensure prefix caching for repeated conversation IDs. If Acme will have many unique session IDs, we should flag that.

2) OpenLlama-13B-4bit: quantized path looks promising but needs 2x memory headroom for the combined KV + streaming windows. For their p95 target we should plan either: (a) dedicated pool with 2x instance count, or (b) recommend they run the heavy extraction as batch jobs (async) and accept higher tail latency.

3) Redwood-7B-ptq as fallback is reasonable. Suggest we default it to "fast-failover" when p95 > 650ms to keep interactive flows within SLO. We'll need a quick QoR (quality of response) guardrail to avoid switching mid-conversation in ways that confuse user experience.

Actionable asks for me:
- Please include a small sample of their transcripts (anonymized) so I can simulate session ID distribution.
- I'll run the prompt_set_v2 through our local rig and drop a simple CSV with p50/p95/throughput numbers and estimated $/1k tokens by Friday morning.

Karthik
Engineering Lead, Inference
Redwood Inference

[inline note: I will instrument a run with batch size ranges 1–8 and 3 different KV cache hit rates (10/50/90%) and include notes on variance.]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca@acme.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot candidate matrix + next asks

Hi Rebecca / Samir — thanks again for your time yesterday. Short external recap and proposed next steps (keeping it actionable):

Recap:
- From our demo, we see two practical pilot paths:
   A) Latency-first (cost-efficient): Redwood-2.7B-q8 — ideal for interactive personalization flows.
   B) Quality-first (precision on extraction): OpenLlama-13B-4bit — stronger accuracy for tricky extraction cases, but higher costs and longer p95 tail (we recommend async workers for heavy jobs).

What we will deliver in the pilot (4 weeks):
- Baseline runs on your anonymized support transcripts using the attached prompt set (prompt_set_v2.zip).
- Per-model p50/p95 latency reports and an estimated $/1k tokens.
- A short quality report against your extraction labels (precision/recall) and a suggested decoding/prompt configuration that minimizes hallucination for billing fields.
- A mutual action plan (MAP-Acme-2027.pdf) listing milestone dates and acceptance criteria.

Asks for Acme:
1) Please confirm the pilot cadence (we suggest sample delivery on Sep 1, test runs Sep 6–10).
2) Share a small anonymized transcript sample (50–100 sessions) and your primary extraction labels so we can run the initial quality pass.
3) Point me to the procurement contact if you want an early billing anchor (we can provide a non-binding pilot quote).

I'll loop Karthik for the benchmarking and Ben for the pricing anchor. If this looks good I can send a one-page SOW and a starter invoice template to procurement.

Thanks,
Jonas
On behalf of Redwood Inference
